top.headline: Rep. Jimmy Gomez to Resign After Ethics Report Finds 'Substantial Evidence' of Sexual Misconduct
top.blurb: The California Democrat will resign Dec. 1 after a bipartisan House Ethics Committee report found substantial evidence he engaged in sexual misconduct toward a staffer, concluding it could constitute criminal sexual assault. Gomez disputes the findings but is stepping down as Democrats prepare to take the House majority.

top.headline: A Private Prison Told ICE Its Jail Was Worth $67 Million. ICE Paid Nearly Half a Billion.
top.blurb: GEO Group valued its Tacoma detention center at $67 million while shopping it; ICE paid roughly $453 million — nearly seven times the appraisal — days after also awarding GEO a $1.5 billion contract to keep running it. GEO plans about $340 million of the proceeds for stock buybacks, and a former DHS inspector general and senators are now asking questions.

top.headline: After Midterm Losses, Republicans Openly Debate What's Next for the Party
top.blurb: Democrats are on track for their biggest House midterm margin since 1992, and Republicans are now openly arguing about life after Trump, with Spencer Cox, Mike Pence and Ted Cruz staking out different directions. The fight will shape the party's identity and its 2028 field.

top.headline: Shiromani Akali Dal and BJP Revive Alliance for Punjab Polls After Six Years
top.blurb: The Shiromani Akali Dal and BJP revived their alliance for Punjab's 2027 Assembly polls at a joint press conference with Sukhbir Badal, Nitin Nabin and Amit Shah, six years after SAD quit the NDA over the farm laws. Seat-sharing is still undecided, but the realignment reshapes the state's political math ahead of the vote.

top.headline: Journalist Saurav Das Says He Was Stopped at Delhi Airport From Travelling to the UK
top.blurb: Journalist and Cockroach Janta Party spokesperson Saurav Das says he was blocked at Delhi airport before a flight to speak at Oxford, Cambridge, LSE and Edinburgh, with reports citing unspecified passport 'discrepancies.' It follows his October arrest over Jantar Mantar protests against the Election Commission's voter-roll revisions.

top.headline: After Four Decades of Political Cartoons, Cartoonists Combine Gets Restricted on Instagram in India
top.blurb: Instagram restricted the account of Cartoonists Combine, a 100-plus-member collective founded in 1983, citing an unnamed government or law-enforcement takedown request under IT Act Section 73(b). The likely trigger: a cartoon depicting Modi as a king controlled by the Chief Election Commissioner.

top.headline: At Least 15 Killed in Ukraine's Kyiv Region as Russia Intensifies Attacks
top.blurb: Russian strikes killed at least 15 people in Ukraine's Kyiv region, including 11 in a collapsed apartment block in Dymer, part of Moscow's vowed harsher response after Ukrainian strikes on the Kerch Bridge. The escalation comes as Ukraine presses the US to release Patriot missiles.

top.headline: Russia Threatens 'Hostile' Estonia With 'Open War'
top.blurb: Moscow accused Estonia, a NATO and EU member, of pushing toward 'open war' after Tallinn announced it will close its Russia border crossings from December 1, citing an alleged Russian-linked arson plot against an Estonian defense firm. Russia also claims Estonia let Ukrainian drones use its airspace, which Tallinn denies.

top.headline: Israeli Strikes Kill at Least Three, Including UNRWA Worker, in Gaza
top.blurb: An Israeli strike near a water well in Jabalia killed UNRWA worker Adel al-Helo; a separate strike on a vehicle in Gaza City killed two more. The deaths underscore how fragile the October 2025 ceasefire remains — at least 1,679 Palestinians have reportedly died since it took effect.

top.headline: Ireland Reach the Emerging Nations Trophy Final, Will Face Unbeaten Sri Lanka
top.blurb: Ireland beat the Netherlands by 44 runs in Ajman, with Lara Maritz unbeaten on 57 and Cara Murray taking 5/17, to finish second in the Super Six and reach the Women's Emerging Nations Trophy final. They face unbeaten leaders Sri Lanka on Wednesday, with captain Gaby Lewis chasing a fourth straight win.

top.headline: Seen at IFFI: Nostalgia Pedro Almodóvar-Style and a Bitter Turkish Delight
top.blurb: At IFFI Goa, Nandini Ramnath reviews two festival titles: Pedro Almodóvar's autofictional 'Bitter Christmas,' about a director mining his own panic attacks and a strained friendship, and Emin Alper's occult Turkish thriller 'Salvation,' about a sheikh trying to stop rival clans sliding into holy war. She finds Almodóvar's usual magic dimmed, Alper's dread-soaked filmmaking genuinely compelling.

bengal.headline: West Bengal Cabinet Clears Proposal to Rename State 'Paschim Banga'
bengal.blurb: Bengal's cabinet approved renaming the state 'Paschim Banga' in both English and Bengali; the proposal goes to the Assembly on December 9, though Parliament has final say.

bengal.headline: Six Months In, Bengal BJP Turns to Cross-Constituency Audits to Rein In Unruly MLAs
bengal.blurb: Facing extortion complaints and factional clashes six months into government, Bengal's BJP will send MLAs to audit counterparts' constituencies under a December 'Seva Doot' drive.

bengal.headline: Calcutta HC Extends Protection to Abhishek Banerjee in Six Criminal Cases
bengal.blurb: The Calcutta High Court extended TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee's protection from arrest in six criminal cases until February 2027, while the state's challenge stays pending at the Supreme Court.

travel.headline: The Caribbean Islands Everyone Falls in Love With
travel.blurb: Lonely Planet picks seven Caribbean islands, from volcanic St Lucia to Dominica's Kalinago heartland, that reward travelers willing to go past the all-inclusive resorts.

travel.headline: Indiana Jones at the Fish Market: A Life Spent Searching for 'Lost Sharks'
travel.blurb: Mongabay profiles marine biologist David Ebert, the 'Lost Shark Guy,' who has spent four decades combing fish markets worldwide and named 56 new shark, ray and chimaera species.

happy.headline: The True Friendship That Saved Abraham Lincoln's Life
happy.blurb: In 1837, a penniless Abraham Lincoln moved into Springfield shopkeeper Joshua Speed's store and shared his bed for nearly four years. When Speed's own wedding loomed, Lincoln spiraled into a suicidal depression at the threat of losing him — and the bond that pulled him back, Smithsonian argues, quietly reshaped the rest of his life.

tech_top.headline: Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO After Scandal Ouster, Senate Testimony Looms
tech_top.blurb: Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO after ousting him weeks earlier over affairs — one allegedly involving a Chinese national — that the board said showed a lack of 'candor.' Elon Musk, Sam Altman and roughly 200,000 petition signers backed his return; Huang now testifies before the Senate Banking Committee on December 3.
tech_top.pm_note: It's a live case study in how fast a governance failure becomes an operational crisis: the executive every AI roadmap in the industry depends on was out, then back in, within weeks, with national-security scrutiny still pending.

tech_top.headline: CrowdStrike to Acquire Zscaler for $43.9B in the Largest-Ever Cybersecurity Merger
tech_top.blurb: CrowdStrike will buy Zscaler in an all-stock deal valuing it at roughly $43.9 billion, pairing endpoint protection with Zscaler's zero-trust network security. The combined company expects over $10 billion in annual recurring revenue and says the deal expands its addressable market by more than $185 billion by 2029, pending regulatory approval.
tech_top.pm_note: Watch the framing — 'expanded addressable market' and multi-year revenue synergies are the standard script for justifying platform-consolidation M&A, and learning to track whether those synergies actually show up is exactly the skeptical lens a PM should bring to any acquisition story.

tech_more.headline: Amazon Buys AI Startup Decart's Optimization Tech for $7.5B to Boost Trainium Chips
tech_more.blurb: Amazon acquired the team behind Decart's AI optimization tech for about $7.5 billion to help its Trainium chips compete with Nvidia.

tech_more.headline: An AI Hacking Tool the FBI Warns About Keeps Spreading Even After Its Creator Pulled It
tech_more.blurb: ARTEX, an open-source tool that lets an AI direct autonomous hacking agents, was pulled from GitHub by its creator, but copies still circulate and the FBI says it's fueling intrusions worldwide.

tech_101.text: An AI 'agent' isn't just a chatbot answering questions — it's a system that takes multi-step actions on its own: deciding what to do next, running tools, and checking its own work. The ARTEX hacking tool wires that same pattern to autonomous intrusion agents that handle reconnaissance, exploitation and data theft end to end, which is why security researchers call it so dangerous even after its creator pulled it.

Zero-trust security assumes no device, user or network location is automatically safe — every request has to prove itself every time, rather than being trusted just because it's 'inside the firewall.' Zscaler built its business on this model; pairing it with CrowdStrike's device-level protection is a bet that endpoint security and zero-trust network access are converging into one product category rather than staying separate markets.

science.headline: Smoke-Affected Hops Have the Biggest Impact on Beer When Added After Fermentation, Study Finds
science.blurb: Oregon State researchers found smoke-tainted hops behave very differently by brewing stage: boiled into the wort, even fully smoke-affected hops were nearly undetectable to tasters, but dry-hopped after fermentation they produced unmistakable barbecue and woodsmoke notes. The chemistry traces to volatile phenols, giving wildfire-hit growers a way to salvage a damaged crop.

science.headline: Two Monster Black Holes From the Dawn of Time Defy Explanation
science.blurb: Astronomers using JWST and Gemini North found the most distant close quasar pair yet seen: two supermassive black holes, 1.5 billion and 400 million solar masses, already merging just 900 million years after the Big Bang. Their size this early defies standard growth models, hinting at an unusually dense, interaction-rich early universe.

science.headline: Mysterious New Viruses Reveal a Missing Link in Evolution
science.blurb: University of Miami researchers scouring genetic databases with AI tools found a new group of viruses that blurs the line between viruses and encapsulins, the protein shells cells use to compartmentalize chemistry. The find suggests the two may have repeatedly evolved from each other rather than one simply begetting the other, complicating a textbook story.

philosophy.headline: Believing and Thinking
philosophy.blurb: Philosophers Neil Van Leeuwen and Jacob Eisler argue church-state separation rests on a real psychological split: 'religious credence,' held voluntarily and shielded from evidence, versus ordinary factual belief, which is involuntary and answers to evidence. The distinction, they say, explains why governments shouldn't impose doctrine while believers still reason evidentially elsewhere.

philosophy.headline: Is Everything Conscious?
philosophy.blurb: Philosopher Sam Kimpton-Nye traces an argument for panpsychism built on the principle of sufficient reason — the idea that everything needs an explanation. If fundamental physical properties must ultimately be explained by something, he argues via thinkers like Hedda Hassel Mørch, that something may have to be consciousness, all the way down.

philosophy.headline: Reason Is More Than a Tool
philosophy.blurb: Philosopher Sasha Mudd warns that defining intelligence as pure optimisation — fine for judging a chess engine — quietly imports a machine model into how we think about human minds. Drawing on Kant against Hume, she argues reason's real job is choosing which ends are worth pursuing, a capacity AI debates risk writing out.

philosophy_101.text: Ordinary belief ('it's raining') tracks evidence and governs your behavior everywhere. 'Religious credence' is a different kind of commitment — one held more voluntarily, largely walled off from counter-evidence and from contexts outside worship. Today's church-state essay uses that split to explain why a government can stay neutral on doctrine while a believer still reasons normally about everything else.

The idea that consciousness isn't something that switches on only inside brains, but is a basic ingredient of physical reality all the way down, present in some minimal form even in particles. Today's essay gets there through the 'principle of sufficient reason': if every fundamental fact needs an explanation, and bare physical properties can't explain themselves, consciousness may be the only candidate left that can.
